reasoning: haad is the Palestinian demonstrative; il- assimilates to the sun letter ل, giving il-loon. mish maashi is the everyday way of saying something doesn't work or won't do.
Palestinian drops the short vowel of the first syllable: kbiir, not kabiir. Covers size and age of a person.
Past tense he-form on the fi3il pattern, fishil. The noun fashal فَشَل is failure; here the pos is verb so fishil is the reading.
ط is emphatic, so a capital T. The vowel is long ee, written with kasra plus ي the way the scheme writes كِيف keef.
ya laTiif calls on God's name al-LaTiif and works as an exclamation of distress. shu plus an adjective is the Palestinian exclamatory frame; 7arr has a shadda so the r doubles.
Young-speaker slang intensifier, as in 7ilu fashkha. Taa marbuta after خ, a back consonant, is a.
Everyday word, so ق is a glottal stop written '. Also used as an insult, but monkey is the base meaning.
Form VIII with the b- present prefix. In this MSA-stratum word urban Palestinian says ذ as z (compare iza, zaki), so the Arabic is respelt with ز for the voice.
Plural shhuur. No case ending in Palestinian, so a bare shahr.
Accurate as MSA, but nobody in Ramallah says istalqa; the conversational verbs are tmaddad or naam. Being an MSA word it keeps [q].
ض is emphatic, so a capital D. Used both for an offer and for a shop promotion, as the English says.
Everyday verb, so ق is a glottal stop; ط is emphatic T. Form III past with the -ni object suffix.
Turkish borrowing, plural kanaadir. Taa marbuta after ر is a.
The conjunction is a bare clitic w in Palestinian, not MSA wa. Before a consonant cluster it surfaces as u, as in ana u inta.
b- plus aakhud gives a long aa; with the -o object suffix the stem vowel drops, baakhdo. أخذ is said with د in Palestinian, which the given spelling already shows.
Long oo, not uu, and ق is a glottal stop in this everyday word.
keef, not kayfa. Form V past plural t3arraftu with the dialect's initial cluster; 3ala ba3D is the fixed reciprocal 'each other'. ض is D.
ق glottalises in this household word. Taa marbuta after ق is a.
Geminate verb: the shadda doubles the emphatic whole, SS. ق is a glottal stop here.
Said as one word with a long uu in the first part; the local pronunciation of the second element is karem rather than classical karm.
illi is the relative pronoun, not the article. 7akeet plus the -o object gives 7akeeto; Sa77 has a shadda so the 7 doubles.
Loanword with two long vowels; plural doolaaraat.
Word-initial hamza sits on a vowel seat, so only the vowel is written. Pain or exasperation interjection; the identically spelt noun akh 'brother' is a different entry.
A learned economic word that Ramallah speakers do use; educated speakers keep ث here, though istismaar with s is also heard.
Long ee in the stressed syllable. In running speech it almost always takes the article, il-kuweet.
